payload.label: L6-F1
payload.text: Report argues thinking blocks are unfaithful (post-hoc), then recommends artifact recording as primary channel—equally self-report and vulnerable to same faithfulness failures. Builds entire adjudication methodology on assumption artifacts ARE truthful. Disconfirmability ('agent claims X but JSONL shows Y') only catches acts, not reasoning. A false artifact claiming 'I declined this because X' cannot be detected even if acts contradict. This is a design risk: if agents write false closures, adjudication corrodes, with no safeguard except manual re-audit of every artifact. Repo gains durability/git-tracking but not reliability.

payload.label: L6-F2
payload.location: §8 'The cost of artifact recording is one line per decision; the cost of thinking-block infrastructure is indefinite maintenance'
payload.text: Report compares recording costs (artifact=one line, thinking=indefinite maintenance). But §6 places 'agent reasoned that X' at Tier 3, reachable only via evidence-chain reconstruction—same labor as artifact audit. Adjudication-time verification cost is invisible while recording-time savings are highlighted. Recommendation succeeds on durability/auditability, not cost. Tradeoff inverts at verification point: cheap to record, expensive to verify. R1-9 flagged this gap; it remains.

payload.label: L6-F3
payload.location: §9 Risk matrix, row 3: 'Silent tool-result truncation corrupts a finding'
payload.text: Report accepts truncation risk 'with disclosure' but proposes no post-hoc detection mechanism. Risk matrix says 'no audit marker exists' and suggests 'compare lengths' as mitigation. But 'compare lengths' requires logging at tool-result time (repo does not do this). At adjudication, truncated result looks identical to complete result. Consequence: finding can silently rest on truncated data. JSONL shows 'tool returned Y' without length record; cannot tell if Y is complete. Accepted disposition leaves a blind spot.

payload.label: L6-F4
payload.location: Open questions #1: 'the single experiment that could overturn the headline'
payload.text: Report identifies OQ1 as critical-path experiment: does showThinkingSummaries:true override the force-omit guard on non-interactive sessions? Was declined because 'writing to settings.json is outside consent.' But the headline rests on this unverified assumption. If the setting DOES work (contrary to code's stated logic), the headline inverts. No safeguard against future config drift; no alert if assumption becomes false. Keystone assumption left untested—not due to technical infeasibility but due to consent friction.

payload.label: L6-F5
payload.location: §9 Risk matrix, row 8: 'Vendor changes default behavior again without a client release | medium | medium | low (re-run the sweep)'
payload.text: Report is version-bound to v2.1.215 read 2026-07-19. Notes history of vendor changes via server-side flag (tengu_quiet_hollow ~2026-03-10) without client release. Proposes 'schedule it, do not engineer around it' as mitigation. But 'schedule' is not a mechanism. No automation alerts if Claude Code upgrades and binary-derived findings decay. Mechanism could change again without detection. Repo has no integrated sweep-on-upgrade hook, no version-check gate, no alert on drift. Mitigation relies on human recall. Time-bomb risk: findings are durable at write-time but have no durability mechanism.

payload.label: L6-F6
payload.location: §3 'Settings and APIs' Compliance API row: '~30 documented activity types, none reasoning'
payload.text: Report concludes 'no reasoning category' based on public surface (30 types enumerated). Lane-1 reported 260+ types, unverified (no enterprise access). Absence claim is bounded to documented surface. Future enterprise deployment could discover reasoning events, retroactively invalidating finding. Open question 10 frames this as curiosity, not risk. Unquantified boundary risk: recommendation depends partly on 'no enterprise reasoning API,' dependency unverified.
